Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
110 AM EDT Mon Oct 19 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 217 PM EDT Sunday...

No significant changes to the current forecast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 217 PM EDT Sunday...

1. A chilly overnight period tonight will be followed by quiet 
and dry weather well into mid week.

2. Dry and seasonable conditions continue through next weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 217 PM EDT Sunday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: High pressure remains overhead this afternoon with some 
channeling enhanced winds in the Champlain and St. Lawrence Valley. 
Winds will continue to remain breezy in the wider valleys through 
tonight, especially across northern New York. A low-level jet 
associated with a broad area of low pressure centered well north 
into the Hudson Bay will bring continued southwest flow to the St. 
Lawrence Valley overnight. Beyond sunset, typical radiational 
cooling process will lower temperatures towards freezing in the 
Northeast Kingdom and near the Connecticut River under clear skies. 
Across northern New York, the low level jet will likely stifle 
radiational cooling conditions with increased flow aloft as well as 
advecting some warmer air, keeping lows in the low to mid 40s for 
the St. Lawrence Valley and the low to mid 30s for most of the 
Adirondacks. South to southwest flow will continue to bring warmer 
air into the region with highs tomorrow into the low 60s. A weak 
moisture starved cold front will slide south from Canada Monday 
night into Tuesday and wash out over the area with no precipitation 
expected, though some morning clouds and cooler temperatures can be 
expected Tuesday morning. Sunny skies will prevail thereafter with 
large scale ridging leading to low humidity and light winds through 
mid week. There continues to be high confidence of no precipitation 
areawide at least through mid week.

KEY MESSAGE 2: A classic stretch of fall weather will continue late 
this week and through the weekend. Surface high pressure will build 
south out of Quebec on Thursday and Friday, bringing cold air 
advection. Highs will drop from the mid-50s to lower 60s on Thursday 
into the upper 40s to around 50 on Friday. The high should be 
centered almost directly overhead over the weekend, leading to clear 
skies, light winds and highs in the 50s. Most mornings will be 
frosty during this stretch, with lows in the 20s and 30s.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Through 06Z Tuesday...Primary aviation hazard will be localized
wind shear at MSS through 10z this morning associated with 2000
feet above ground jet of 35 to 40 knots. Otherwise, high
confidence of VFR conditions prevailing the next 24 hours at all
TAF sites, with south to southwest winds 5 to 15 knots. 

Outlook...

Tuesday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Wednesday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Wednesday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Thursday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Thursday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Friday: VFR. NO SIG WX.

&&

.MARINE...
A Lake Wind Advisory remains in effect for the Broad and Northern 
Waters of Lake Champlain through tonight. Channeling effects are 
leading to minor enhancement of winds to 20 to 25 knots and waves 
throughout the day from 1 to 3 feet for the Broad and Northern 
Waters. Winds may weaken slightly to 15 to 20 knots on the Broad 
Water during the the afternoon today, but gusts are expected to 
remain near 25 knots and sustained winds are expected to increase 
again to 20 to 25 knots towards late this afternoon and evening, and 
continue through tonight.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&

$$
